display.purpose: Hero headlines on the marketing landing only. Cormorant Garamond at 600, tracked tight.

headline.purpose: Section openers on landing, page titles in portals at desktop sizes.

title.purpose: Card titles, dialog titles, dashboard widget titles.

body.purpose: All paragraph text. Manrope 400, line-height 1.6, max 65–75ch in long-form.

label.purpose: Buttons, nav links, form labels. Slight positive tracking signals interactivity.

shadows.name: shadow-soft
shadows.purpose: Default card shadow at rest. Reads as paper-on-paper, not paper-on-floor.

shadows.name: shadow-soft-lg
shadows.purpose: Hover state for elevated cards and resting modal lift.

shadows.name: shadow-modal
shadows.purpose: Modal dialog shadow when sitting over a blurred backdrop. The only theatrical shadow in the system.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Default exponential ease-out for state transitions. Replaces the looser linear ease-out on existing animations.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Button and link hover/focus state transitions.

components.name: Modal Dialog
components.description: Champagne surface over a charcoal-tinted backdrop with backdrop-filter blur. The only place a theatrical shadow lives.

New Note

Write a note for the dancer. Notes can be private, shared with the student, or shared with the guardian.
components.css: .ds-modal-backdrop { position: fixed; inset: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 1rem; background: rgba(10, 10, 10, 0.5); backdrop-filter: blur(4px); animation: ds-fadeIn 300ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1); } .ds-modal { background: #faf8f5; color: #1a1a1a; border-radius: 0.5rem; box-shadow: 0 20px 60px rgba(10, 10, 10, 0.18); width: 100%; max-width: 32rem; animation: ds-slideUp 300ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1); display: flex; flex-direction: column; max-height: 90vh; overflow: hidden; } .ds-modal-header { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding: 1.25rem 1.5rem; border-bottom: 1px solid #ebe4d8; } .ds-modal-title { font-family: 'Cormorant Garamond', Georgia, Garamond, serif; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.25; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: #0a0a0a; margin: 0; } .ds-modal-close { background: transparent; border: none; color: #4d4d4d; cursor: pointer; padding: 0.25rem; border-radius: 0.25rem; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; transition: background 200ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1), color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1); } .ds-modal-close svg { width: 18px; height: 18px; } .ds-modal-close:hover { background: #f5f1ea; color: #1a1a1a; } .ds-modal-body { padding: 1.5rem; font-family: 'Manrope', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.6; letter-spacing: 0.01em; overflow-y: auto; } @keyframes ds-fadeIn { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } } @keyframes ds-slideUp { from { transform: translateY(20px); opacity: 0; } to { transform: translateY(0); opacity: 1; } }

narrative.overview: A printed program book from a serious classical season: champagne-paper stock, charcoal serif headlines, a single rose accent that reads as a velvet curtain ribbon, gilt detailing reserved for premium acts. The interface treats every screen as a page in that program. Generous margins. Considered hierarchy. Nothing shouts. The visual language is borrowed from Lincoln Center programs and editorial dance journals, not from SaaS marketing pages. The system is restrained but not austere. Warmth comes from the champagne paper tone (off-white tinted toward gold) rather than from playful color or rounded geometry. Precision comes from typography: a single confident serif for display, a humanist sans for body, both tracked tightly. The aesthetic is feminine in the way classical performance is feminine, not in the way a stock-photo template is. There is no gradient, no glow, no glassmorphism. This system explicitly rejects the SaaS dashboard idiom, the heavy promotional landing page, and the low-end dance-studio website family.
keyCharacteristics: Champagne paper as the surface, never #fff white.
Stage rose as a single confident accent, never a gradient.
Cormorant Garamond carries every heading; Manrope carries every paragraph.
Soft shadows or none; depth is rare and quiet.
Borders are champagne stroke at 1px; never a colored side stripe.

rules.name: The One Ribbon Rule
rules.body: Stage Rose is the ribbon, not the wallpaper. It appears on no more than ~10% of any screen at rest. Curtain Gilt is similarly rare; the two never compete for attention on the same surface.

rules.name: The No-White Rule
rules.body: #fff is forbidden anywhere a surface or text is intended to be neutral. Champagne Silk is white. Component code that says bg-white or text-white against a colored background is tech debt, not a design choice.

rules.name: The No-Black Rule
rules.body: #000 is forbidden. Modal scrims use rgba(10, 10, 10, 0.5) with backdrop-blur, not rgba(0,0,0,0.5). Stage Black is the deepest ink available.

rules.name: The No Side-Stripe Rule
rules.body: Colored border-left greater than 1px is forbidden as a card or alert affordance. Rich-text blockquotes inside the editor are the single sanctioned exception.

rules.name: The Serif-For-Headings Rule
rules.body: Every h1 through h6 uses Cormorant Garamond, in every component, in every portal. No exceptions.

rules.name: The Tight-Tracking Rule
rules.body: Display and Headline are negatively tracked. Body is slightly positively tracked. Labels are positively tracked further. The tracking ladder is part of the hierarchy; do not flatten it.

rules.name: The No-All-Caps Rule
rules.body: Headings are never set in ALL CAPS. The display serif does not survive uppercase.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface with no shadow is the correct default. Add shadow-soft only when a card needs to read as a discrete paper artifact against the champagne page; otherwise let the border carry it.

rules.name: The No-Drop-Shadow-On-Buttons Rule
rules.body: Buttons do not carry shadows at rest. The gold button variant is the single exception, because Curtain Gilt is itself a premium signal and the shadow underlines that.

dos: Do use Champagne Silk (#faf8f5) as the page surface and Champagne Page (#f5f1ea) for any raised area.
Do apply the global border-color: champagne-stroke rule. Borders are 1px Champagne Stroke unless a component spec overrides.
Do set every heading in Cormorant Garamond, every paragraph and label in Manrope.
Do reserve Stage Rose for one accent role per screen, used on <=10% of the surface.
Do use Curtain Gilt only on premium-gated affordances. Never as decoration.
Do swap surfaces by tonal layer (Silk on Page, Page on Silk) instead of by adding shadows.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion on every animation declared in globals.css.
Do maintain 44px minimum touch targets on dancer-facing mobile UI.
donts: Don't use #fff or #000. Champagne Silk replaces white; Stage Black replaces black.
Don't ship the SaaS dashboard idiom: KPI-card grids, gradient hero metrics, sidebar with monochrome icons, 'Welcome back' greetings.
Don't ship the heavy promotional site idiom on the landing: parallax, testimonial carousels, 'Trusted by' rows, gradient mesh hero, sticky CTA bars.
Don't ship the low-end dance studio idiom: script fonts, stock dancer silhouettes, autoplay music, pink-on-pink with no contrast, ribbon dividers, 'Welcome to our family!' copy.
Don't ship gamification chrome: streaks, badges, levels, 'you crushed it!', confetti.
Don't use a colored border-left greater than 1px as a card or alert accent. The TipTap blockquote rule is the single sanctioned exception.
Don't use gradient text. Solid color, weight contrast for emphasis.
Don't use glassmorphism as decoration. The modal backdrop's blur is purposeful; do not reach for blurred-glass cards in resting UI.
Don't nest cards. A card inside a card is always wrong.
Don't rely on raw Tailwind grays (gray-50..gray-900) when a Charcoal or Champagne family value is available.
Don't add a 'modal as first thought' pattern. Try inline reveal, slide-over, or in-page editing first.
Don't use uppercase set in Cormorant Garamond for headings.
Don't introduce any color outside the four families (Champagne, Charcoal, Ballet Pink/Rose, Gold) without naming it as a new system role.
